# Power Manager Slow FSM Behavioral Specification

## 1. Overview

The power manager slow FSM is responsible for the power-on and power-off sequencing of the main power domain, the associated isolation clamps, and the clock enables for the main system clocks. It operates from an always-on slow clock and is the first sequencer to run after a power-on reset.

It also manages the transition into and out of low-power states, detects wakeup and reset requests while in low power, records the power-up cause, and monitors main power stability.

## 2. Power-On Reset Behavior

After power-on reset, the module shall:

- Drive the main power control to the powered-on state.
- Keep all isolation clamps asserted.
- Keep all main clock enables deasserted.
- Not assert the power-up request.
- Report the power-up cause as a power-on reset.

The module shall then wait until the main power-ok indication confirms that the main power rail is stable. It shall not proceed past this point until that condition is satisfied.

## 3. Power-Up Sequencing

Once main power is stable, the module shall release the isolation clamps in the correct order:

- First deassert the environment isolation clamp.
- Then deassert the main isolation clamp.

After the clamps are released, the module shall:

- Enable the core and I/O clock enables.
- Enable the USB clock enable according to the active-mode USB clock configuration.
- Wait until all clocks that are expected to be running report valid.

Once all required clock-valid indications are present, the module shall assert the power-up request output. It shall hold this request until:

- The power-up acknowledge input is asserted, and
- No power-down request is pending.

When both conditions are met, the module shall deassert the power-up request and enter the idle state.

In the idle state, the module shall keep main power on and keep the active clock configuration enabled.

## 4. Power-Down and Low-Power Entry

From the idle state, when a power-down request is asserted and no power-up acknowledgement is outstanding, the module shall:

- Assert the power-down acknowledgement output.
- Hold that acknowledgement until the power-down request is deasserted.

After the power-down acknowledgement handshake completes, the module shall enter the power-down sequence.

During power-down sequencing, the module shall:

- Change the clock enable outputs from their active configuration to their low-power configuration.
- Wait until all clocks that are configured to be disabled in low power report that they are actually off.
- If main power is configured to remain on, keep main power on and proceed to the low-power state without asserting the isolation clamps.
- If main power is configured to be turned off:
  - Assert the environment isolation clamp first.
  - Assert the main isolation clamp.
  - Drive the main power control to the powered-off state.
  - Wait until the main power-ok indication goes low.
  - Then enter the low-power state.

If the low-power configuration keeps main power on, the module shall not wait for main power-ok to go low.

## 5. Low-Power State

In the low-power state, the module shall maintain the power, isolation, and clock-enable outputs as configured for low power.

While in low power, the module shall monitor the wakeup and reset request inputs. Either condition shall cause the module to exit low power and begin the power-up sequence.

The behavior shall be as follows:

- If only a wakeup is asserted, the power-up cause shall be reported as wakeup.
- If a reset request is asserted, the power-up cause shall be reported as reset.
- If both are asserted, the reset cause shall take priority.

Each exit from low power shall invert the power-up cause toggle output. This provides a change indication whenever a new low-power exit occurs.

## 6. Wakeup and Reset Request Observation

The wakeup and reset request inputs shall be observed only while the module is in the low-power state. They shall be ignored during all other sequencing states.

A reset request received in low power shall be treated as a low-power exit trigger, with the only difference from a wakeup being the recorded power-up cause.

## 7. Main Power Stability Monitoring

The module shall begin monitoring the main power-ok indication only after it has observed main power as stable during a power-up sequence.

Once monitoring is active, it shall continue while main power is expected to be on, including active operation and low-power states where main power remains on.

If the main power-ok indication drops while monitoring is active, the module shall assert a reset request output. The reset request shall remain asserted until cleared by the clear-request input.

If the module has requested main power to be turned off, monitoring shall be disabled. This prevents the expected loss of main power during a deep low-power state from generating an internal reset request.

The reset request output generated by main power instability is distinct from the reset request input used as a low-power wakeup cause.

## 8. Invalid State Behavior

If the module’s internal FSM enters an invalid or unrecoverable state, the module shall:

- Assert the invalid status output.
- Drive the main power control to the powered-off state.
- Assert all isolation clamps.
- Force all main clock enable outputs to the enabled state.
- Remain in this terminal state until a power-on reset.

The module shall not attempt to resume normal sequencing after entering this state.

## 9. Clock Enable Outputs

The module shall control the main clock enable outputs as follows:

- During power-up and idle, core and I/O clock enables shall be asserted.
- During low power, core and I/O clock enables shall follow the low-power configuration, provided main power remains on.
- If main power is turned off, all main-domain clock enables shall be deasserted.
- The USB clock enable during power-up and idle shall follow the active-mode USB configuration.
- The USB clock enable during low power shall follow the low-power USB configuration, qualified by whether main power remains on.
- During the invalid state, all clock enable outputs shall be forced to the enabled state.

## 10. USB Clock Enable Handshake Behavior

The module shall provide both a USB IP clock enable output and a separate USB clock enable output to the analog clock controller.

The USB IP clock enable output shall reflect the internally requested USB clock state.

The analog-side USB clock enable shall be asserted whenever the internally requested USB clock state is enabled. When the internally requested USB clock state is disabled, the analog-side output shall remain asserted while the USB clock status input indicates that the USB clock is still active. Only after the USB clock status input indicates that the clock is inactive shall the analog-side USB clock enable be deasserted.

## 11. Isolation Clamp Behavior

The module shall generate two isolation clamp controls:

- An environment isolation clamp.
- A main isolation clamp.

During power-up, the environment clamp shall be deasserted before the main clamp.

During power-down, when main power is to be removed, the environment clamp shall be asserted before the main clamp.

When main power is configured to remain on, both clamps shall remain deasserted during low power. During the invalid state, both clamps shall be asserted.

## 12. Power-Up Cause Output

The module shall provide a power-up cause output and a cause toggle output.

The power-up cause shall be:

- Power-on reset after a power-on reset.
- Wakeup after a low-power exit caused by a wakeup.
- Reset after a low-power exit caused by a reset request.

The cause toggle output shall invert on every low-power exit and shall remain stable while the module is in low power or in the power-up sequence.
